catalysts.headline: Agreed to sell a second Priority Review Voucher for $210 million (announcement, not yet closed as of this report), this one tied to the Genglycos (DTX401) approval for glycogen storage disease type Ia; buyer undisclosed, sale subject to Hart-Scott-Rodino and other customary closing conditions. Combined with the Oct 14 FAYUVI-linked PRV sale, the two deals total roughly $413M.

catalysts.headline: FDA granted full approval of FAYUVI (UX111, rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf) gene therapy, the first-ever approved treatment for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A (MPS IIIA); Ultragenyx received a Priority Review Voucher
catalysts.impact: shares jumped ~12.6-13%, with further gains after-hours

catalysts.headline: Ultragenyx's Phase 3 ASPIRE study of apazunersen (GTX-102) in Angelman syndrome missed its primary endpoint (change from baseline in Bayley-4 cognitive raw score) and its key secondary endpoint (Multidomain Responder Index net response); safety was consistent with the earlier Phase 1/2 data. Company said it is evaluating the program's disposition and will implement 'significant' expense reductions.
catalysts.impact: Shares fell approximately 44-46% (reported variously, e.g. close of $14.84 vs prior close, down $11.68/-44%); JPMorgan downgraded to Neutral from Overweight and cut its price target to $36 from $80; Evercore cut its target to $16; this appears NOT to be reflected in the on-file market cap/EPS figures, which are dated Aug 20, 2026 (pre-crash) — see conflicts

catalysts.headline: FDA approved GENGLYCOS gene therapy (Ultragenyx's other 2026 approval), which also came with a Priority Review Voucher
Q2 2026 results: record quarterly revenue $214M; net loss $92M / $0.90 per share; FY2026 revenue guidance $730M-$760M

conflicts: On-file market cap ($2.6B, as of 2026-08-20) and sharesOutstanding-derived price level predate the Sept 2, 2026 ~44-46% single-day drop following the failed Phase 3 ASPIRE (apazunersen/GTX-102) readout; the on-file Oct 9 price of $15.45 is consistent with a post-crash level, implying a market cap closer to ~$1.5B (98.4M shares x $15.45) rather than the stale $2.6B figure. Not reconciled/recalculated with a verified current share count this session — flagging rather than recomputing.

DTX401/GENGLYCOS is confirmed (via company/press materials) to be the same product under two names (DTX401 = development code, GENGLYCOS/pariglasgene brecaparvovec-opnr = approved brand name for glycogen storage disease type Ia) — this clarifies, but does not change, the on-file Aug 19, 2026 GENGLYCOS approval catalyst (FDA's PDUFA date for DTX401 was Aug 23, 2026; approval reporting is inconsistently dated Aug 19-20 across sources).
notes: Company has not yet announced a final decision on the apazunersen/GTX-102 program's disposition (still under review as of the latest coverage found, early-to-mid Sept 2026); a related AURORA study in other Angelman genotypes is also in question per analyst commentary. No October 2026 update to this decision, and no confirmation of specific cost-cutting dollar figures or headcount, found this session. Next-earnings estimates now point to Nov 3, 2026 (EarningsWhispers/The Right Trader) rather than the on-file Nov 4 — still not company-confirmed either way; not overwriting the on-file date given both are unconfirmed estimates, flagging the discrepancy here instead.
